title: DSA Zero to Hero in Python
description: Comprehensive 16-week DSA curriculum for Python developers preparing for tech interviews. Part 1 covers foundations, arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, binary search, sliding window, hash tables, and binary trees.
goal: Master core data structures, visual mental models, and solve foundational LeetCode Easy and Medium problems in Python.
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
audience: Software engineering intern and new-grad candidates learning DSA in Python.

sources.title: Data Structures Easy to Advanced Course (William Fiset)

modules.title: Foundations, Big-O & Array Memory
modules.summary: Asymptotic time and space complexity, static vs dynamic memory allocation, and array mechanics.

modules.title: Linked Lists, Stacks & Monotonic Patterns
modules.summary: Pointer-based lists, LIFO/FIFO structures, call stacks, and monotonic stack patterns.

modules.title: Binary Search, Sliding Window & Hash Tables
modules.summary: Logarithmic range reduction, two-pointer sliding windows, and hash collision resolution.

modules.title: Binary Trees, BSTs & Traversals
modules.summary: Tree hierarchy, DFS/BFS traversals, BST invariants, and binary tree problem patterns.

tasks.title: Big-O Time Complexity Foundations
tasks.description: Watch the asymptotic notation chapter of William Fiset's course. Learn definitions for O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2), and O(2^n). Practice simplifying complexity expressions by dropping constant factors and keeping dominant terms.
objectives: Explain asymptotic upper bounds using Big-O notation
Simplify complexity expressions using constant dropping and dominant term rules
Identify the time complexity of single loops, nested loops, and binary search operations
tradeoffs: Worst-case Big-O gives upper-bound guarantees vs average-case behavior which reflects typical inputs
verificationQuestions: Why do we drop constant multipliers like 3n into O(n)?
What is the time complexity of nested loops where the inner loop runs n times and outer loop runs n times?

tasks.title: Space Complexity & Array Memory Layouts
tasks.description: Learn auxiliary space complexity and contiguous memory layout of static vs dynamic arrays. Understand how CPU cache locality benefits sequential array indexing and analyze the amortized O(1) time complexity of dynamic array capacity doubling.
objectives: Differentiate auxiliary space complexity from total space complexity
Explain contiguous memory layout and indexing offset arithmetic
Derive the amortized O(1) time bound for dynamic array resizing
tradeoffs: Contiguous arrays provide O(1) random access via indexing but require contiguous memory reallocation during resizes
verificationQuestions: Why is index lookup in an array an O(1) operation?
What happens to memory when a dynamic array exceeds its capacity?

tasks.title: Two Sum
tasks.description: Solve Two Sum in Python. Start with the O(n^2) brute force solution, then optimize to O(n) time using a Python dictionary (hash map) to store values and their indices in a single pass.

tasks.title: Contains Duplicate
tasks.description: Solve Contains Duplicate in Python. Compare an O(n log n) sorting solution against an O(n) hash set solution in terms of time and space trade-offs.

tasks.title: Valid Anagram
tasks.description: Solve Valid Anagram in Python. Implement character frequency counting using a hash map or fixed-size array of size 26.

tasks.title: Valid Palindrome
tasks.description: Solve Valid Palindrome using the two-pointer technique in Python. Initialize left and right pointers at opposite ends of the string and converge toward the center while filtering alphanumeric characters.

tasks.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
tasks.description: Solve Two Sum II on a sorted array using left and right pointers to achieve O(n) time and O(1) space complexity.

practice.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

tasks.title: Singly and Doubly Linked List Mechanics
tasks.description: Watch William Fiset's chapter on Singly and Doubly Linked Lists. Study node structures, head/tail pointer tracking, O(1) prepending/appending, and O(n) traversal. Implement a custom Singly Linked List class in Python.
objectives: Implement a node class and linked list class with head and tail pointers
Compare time complexities of array vs linked list operations
Perform pointer reversals without losing reference to neighboring nodes
tradeoffs: Linked lists allow O(1) insertions/deletions at known positions without memory shift but lack O(1) random access and incur pointer memory overhead
verificationQuestions: Why is search in a linked list O(n) while in a static array it is O(1) by index?
How does a doubly linked list enable O(1) deletion of a node given its reference?

resources.title: Singly and Doubly Linked Lists Chapter

tasks.title: Reverse Linked List
tasks.description: Solve Reverse Linked List in Python both iteratively (using prev, curr, next pointers) and recursively. Verify space complexities O(1) iterative vs O(n) call stack recursive.

tasks.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
tasks.description: Solve Merge Two Sorted Lists in Python using a dummy head node and pointer comparison loops.

tasks.title: Linked List Cycle
tasks.description: Solve Linked List Cycle using Floyd's Tortoise and Hare two-pointer algorithm in Python to achieve O(n) time and O(1) space.

tasks.title: Stacks & Queues (LIFO & FIFO Mechanics)
tasks.description: Watch William Fiset's Stacks and Queues chapters. Study Last-In First-Out (LIFO) stack operations and First-In First-Out (FIFO) queue operations. Implement a stack using Python lists and a queue using collections.deque.
objectives: Explain LIFO and FIFO invariants and their runtime complexities
Identify real-world stack applications including call stacks and expression parsing
Implement stacks and queues using Python collections
tradeoffs: Python list as a stack is fast for append/pop at end, but inefficient O(n) for queue pop(0) due to memory shifts; deque provides O(1) at both ends
verificationQuestions: Why should you use collections.deque instead of a standard list for queue operations in Python?
How does recursion rely on an implicit call stack?

tasks.title: Valid Parentheses
tasks.description: Solve Valid Parentheses using a stack and a hash map for matching closing brackets to opening brackets in Python.

tasks.title: Min Stack
tasks.description: Design a stack that supports getMin() in O(1) time using an auxiliary minimum stack to track minimum values alongside main stack pushes.

tasks.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
tasks.description: Evaluate postfix mathematical expressions using a stack in Python, handling integer division truncation rules.

tasks.title: Daily Temperatures
tasks.description: Solve Daily Temperatures using a monotonic decreasing stack in Python to find the number of days until a warmer temperature in O(n) time.

tasks.title: Binary Search Principles & Integer Overflow
tasks.description: Study logarithmic range reduction algorithm for sorted arrays. Understand midpoint calculation mid = left + (right - left) // 2 to prevent overflow, and learn boundary adjustments for exact search vs lower/upper bound insertion points.
objectives: Explain logarithmic time complexity O(log n) derivation
Implement bug-free binary search loops avoiding infinite loops
Identify sorted array properties that allow binary search applicability
tradeoffs: Binary search requires O(n log n) initial sorting overhead but yields fast O(log n) lookups across dynamic queries
verificationQuestions: Why does binary search require a sorted input array?
How do you update left and right pointers when target > nums[mid]?

tasks.title: Binary Search
tasks.description: Solve standard Binary Search on a sorted array of integers in Python.

tasks.title: Search a 2D Matrix
tasks.description: Treat an m x n matrix as a virtual 1D sorted array and apply binary search using index mapping row = mid // n and col = mid % n.

tasks.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
tasks.description: Apply modified binary search to identify which half of the rotated array is sorted and determine if the target lies within the sorted half.

tasks.title: Sliding Window Pattern & Two Pointers
tasks.description: Study fixed-size and dynamic-size sliding window techniques. Learn how maintaining running window counts converts naive O(n^2) subarray problems into optimal O(n) solutions.
objectives: Identify contiguous subarray and substring problems suitable for sliding window
Implement fixed-size window movement
Implement dynamic window expansion and contraction based on condition bounds
tradeoffs: Sliding window reduces O(n^2) brute force nested loops to O(n) linear scans by tracking state changes at window boundaries
verificationQuestions: When should you shrink the left pointer of a sliding window?
What is the difference between fixed and variable size sliding windows?

tasks.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
tasks.description: Track the minimum price seen so far and calculate maximum profit achievable in a single pass O(n) time.

practice.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

tasks.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
tasks.description: Use a dynamic sliding window with a set or dictionary to maintain a substring of unique characters in O(n) time.

tasks.title: Hash Table Collisions & Load Factors
tasks.description: Watch William Fiset's Hash Tables chapter. Study hash functions, bucket arrays, separate chaining (linked lists), and open addressing (linear/quadratic probing). Understand load factor limits and table resizing.
objectives: Explain separate chaining vs open addressing collision strategies
Define load factor alpha = n / k and how it triggers table expansion
Analyze average O(1) vs worst-case O(n) hash table operations
tradeoffs: Separate chaining handles high load factors gracefully using extra pointer memory; open addressing keeps memory contiguous but degrades quickly if load factor exceeds 0.7
verificationQuestions: Why does a high load factor degrade hash table performance?
What is a hash collision and how does separate chaining resolve it?

tasks.title: Group Anagrams
tasks.description: Group words by their character count tuple key using a Python collections.defaultdict in O(n * k) time.

tasks.title: Top K Frequent Elements
tasks.description: Count element frequencies using a hash map, then use Bucket Sort array indices to collect top K frequent numbers in O(n) time.

tasks.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
tasks.description: Convert array to a hash set, then identify sequence starts (num - 1 not in set) to build consecutive sequences in O(n) overall time.

tasks.title: Binary Tree Structure & DFS Traversals
tasks.description: Watch William Fiset's Binary Trees chapter. Learn tree terminology (root, leaf, height, depth) and DFS recursive traversals: Pre-order (Root, Left, Right), In-order (Left, Root, Right), and Post-order (Left, Right, Root).
objectives: Define node height, depth, and binary tree invariants
Implement recursive Pre-order, In-order, and Post-order traversals in Python
Recognize how In-order traversal visits nodes of a BST in sorted order
tradeoffs: Recursive DFS traversals are intuitive and use implicit call stack memory O(h), but risk StackOverflow on deep skewed trees
verificationQuestions: In what order does an In-order traversal visit nodes in a Binary Search Tree?
What is the space complexity of tree recursion on a completely skewed tree vs a balanced tree?

tasks.title: Invert Binary Tree
tasks.description: Swap left and right subtrees recursively for every node in a binary tree in Python.

tasks.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
tasks.description: Calculate maximum depth of a binary tree using post-order DFS: 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)).

tasks.title: Diameter of Binary Tree
tasks.description: Compute the longest path between any two nodes by updating a global maximum left_height + right_height during DFS traversal.

tasks.title: Balanced Binary Tree
tasks.description: Check height balance condition abs(left - right) <= 1 bottom-up in O(n) time by returning -1 on imbalance.

tasks.title: BFS Level-Order Traversal Mechanics
tasks.description: Learn Breadth-First Search (BFS) level-order traversal on trees using a FIFO queue (collections.deque). Track level sizes during iterations to group nodes level by level.
objectives: Explain queue-based level order traversal algorithm
Process tree nodes level by level using queue snapshot sizes
Contrast memory requirements of BFS vs DFS on wide vs deep trees
tradeoffs: BFS requires O(w) queue space bounded by maximum tree width, whereas DFS requires O(h) space bounded by tree height
verificationQuestions: How do you ensure nodes from different levels are separated into distinct lists during level-order traversal?
When would BFS be preferable to DFS on a tree structure?

tasks.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
tasks.description: Implement level-order traversal using collections.deque in Python to return a list of values grouped level by level.

tasks.title: BST Invariants, Search & Validation
tasks.description: Study Binary Search Tree property: all_left < node.val < all_right. Learn range-based validation [min_val, max_val] and logarithmic O(log n) search and insertion on balanced BSTs.
objectives: State the global BST invariant across subtrees
Validate BST correctness using range boundaries min_val and max_val
Explain why naive validation (node.left < node < node.right) fails for invalid BSTs
tradeoffs: Balanced BSTs offer O(log n) search, insertion, and deletion, but degenerate to O(n) linked lists if keys are inserted in sorted order without rebalancing
verificationQuestions: Why is checking left.val < root.val < right.val insufficient to validate a BST?
What is the in-order traversal result of a valid BST?

tasks.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
tasks.description: Validate BST property using DFS with min and max bounds passed down recursion branches in Python.

tasks.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
tasks.description: Find LCA in a BST by leveraging node values: if both p and q are smaller than root, move left; if larger, move right; otherwise root is LCA.

practice.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree

tasks.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
tasks.description: Perform an iterative or recursive In-order traversal on a BST to find the K-th visited element in O(k) time.

practice.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
